facts.fact: Tchadinfos reports that under the TASDJIL project new birth certificates carry a national identification number (NNI), with the data held on the servers of the secured titles agency ANATS, which issues the ID documents.
TECHNIDEV's director general says civil registry desks have been set up in more than 50 maternity units under TASDJIL, with the aim of covering all health facilities.

TCD.note: No count or share of people holding a national ID is given.

facts.fact: Tchadinfos says that under TASDJIL a child's new birth certificate contains a national identification number (NNI), with registration desks in more than 50 maternity units and the aim of covering all health facilities; older certificates carry no NNI.

TCD.note: The document does not say who operates, maintains or owns the ID system.
No public register keyed on the ID number is named.

facts.fact: Tchadinfos says ANATS is the agency that issues digitised identity documents and that new birth certificates carry a national identification number (NNI).
Tchadinfos says births are registered digitally under TASDJIL from the maternity, with state civil registry desks set up in more than 50 maternity units.
TECHNIDEV's director general says civil registry desks have been set up in more than 50 maternity units, with no total of offices given.
